title: The Whispering Sands — Keeper's Field Chart

orientation.overview: A wooded island with a high northern lighthouse, a sheltered southeastern wreck beach and a western ferry harbour. The eastern shelf is cut by a tidal channel; the western coast is mostly steep rock.
orientation.scale: Schematic: coordinates are drawing positions, not puzzle-grid coordinates or measured distances.
orientation.travel_policy: Travel minutes are approximate story pacing. Do not impose a classroom countdown or subtract time for an incorrect answer.
orientation.gate_policy: Use solved server evidence. Gates mark available records and safe mechanisms, never shelter or a real-time deadline. Safe exploration may approach the same evidence by another route but cannot replace its joint solution. A gate does not itself move the party or advance a chapter.

nodes.label: Wreck Beach
nodes.terrain: Sheltered southeastern sand, driftwood and the broken family boat.
nodes.dm_note: Harbour chest 07 washed down from the island camp store; it is not from the family boat. The dry path to Palm Camp is open before its equipment drawer is solved.

nodes.label: Palm Camp
nodes.terrain: A sandy terrace above high water, with an open store porch, roof and drinking water.
nodes.dm_note: Immediate safe shelter and recovery, even with the chest locked. The packing puzzle gates supplies and crossing information, never access to this porch.

nodes.label: Nine-Stone Crossing
nodes.terrain: Nine exposed stones in a shallow eastern channel; the crossing is submerged at high tide.
nodes.dm_note: A local 3 × 3 evidence chart resolves the marked passage. Neither the island map nor a physical roll identifies the correct stones. Keep the route secret until both seats have submitted successfully.

nodes.label: Old Stone Arch
nodes.terrain: Weathered masonry at the northern end of the tidal shelf, opening into a fern gully.
nodes.dm_note: The keeper's records are discovered beneath the arch after the crossing lock is solved. The gully leads a short distance inland to the archive.

nodes.label: Keeper's Archive
nodes.terrain: A low stone vault under the central ridge, entered from the fern gully.
nodes.dm_note: The chronology combines independent witnesses. Only its solved discovery reveals the recorder and witnessed access receipt. Do not add a motive before the later letter is recovered.

nodes.label: Voice Machine
nodes.terrain: A brass apparatus in the lower chamber of the hilltop lighthouse.
nodes.dm_note: The lower oil test lamp and brazier are separate from the upper electric beacon. Restoration returns voices and makes the signal circuit safe; it does not make a rescue call.

nodes.label: Beacon Gallery
nodes.terrain: The glazed lantern and open gallery above the voice-machine chamber.
nodes.dm_note: Compare signal channel and permission records after restoration. The final lock prepares a plan; a later explicit ending action records the free call and boarding. A silent hand key is available.

nodes.label: Ferry Quay
nodes.terrain: A sheltered western harbour and a wooden pier beneath the headland.
nodes.dm_note: The final lock prepares the signal, but only the explicit ending flow records its use and boarding. Confrontation, forgiveness and leaving without reconciliation all permit rescue.

edges.tide: Any tide; camp is above high water.
edges.description: Walk up the short dry rise to the open porch and water. Safe shelter is available immediately, before opening the equipment drawer.

edges.tide: Approach is safe at any tide; the exposed stones require falling or low water.
edges.description: The recovered chart enables investigation of the marked crossing. Scouting the nearby strand is safe beforehand; the gate concerns useful route evidence, not leaving shelter.

edges.tide: Low or falling water. At high water wait safely; never erase a solved route.
edges.description: Use the jointly established safe route during a low-water window. Scouting or alternative approaches may bring the party to these same records; a physical roll cannot replace the evidence.

edges.tide: Dry ground once beyond the crossing.
edges.description: Walk inland through the fern gully to the archive beneath the ridge. The discovered records are examined here.

edges.tide: Dry ridge path, above all ordinary tides.
edges.description: Carry the seal along the dry ridge to the lower lighthouse chamber after comparing the archive records. A misplaced seal is recovered by its tether, not replaced with a new talisman.
The restored circuit makes the upper gallery safe. The beacon still needs a fresh, freely initiated distress signal.

edges.tide: Dry western descent; the sheltered pier supports boarding at either tide.
edges.description: Once the signal plan is solved, use the explicit ending flow to make the chosen call and board. Forgiveness is never a boarding requirement.

tide_rules.initial_state: Falling after the storm; a low-water window can follow the pair's preparation.
tide_rules.dm_policy: Use the tide for atmosphere and safe planning. It is not a real-time deadline or punishment for English mistakes. Once both submissions are accepted, provide a safe crossing window. Never trap the pair between tides or undo accepted evidence.

sightlines.visibility: Clear view of the nearby palm terrace and shelter sites.
The lighthouse lantern is a tiny silhouette above the northern ridge; the internal machine and its labels are invisible.
The arch appears beyond the channel when mist thins. Sight does not establish the correct local route.
The lighthouse roof appears only after leaving the vault and climbing beyond the forest saddle.
An unobstructed western view over the sheltered harbour, the pier and the ferry approach.
The lantern crowns the headland and its restored signal is plainly visible.
